simple: Your own type that bundles data with the only functions allowed to change it.
analogy: A kitchen station: the shelf, its rule card and the one cook who works it.
precise: A user-defined type declared with class or struct, containing data members and member functions; with class the members are private unless marked otherwise.
source: D1, D2 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: One real thing made from a class, with its own data.
analogy: One actual soup shelf, built to the station plan.
precise: A region of storage with a type and a lifetime; each object of class type has its own copy of the non-static data members.
source: D2 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R5 of F2-09

simple: A variable that lives inside each object.
analogy: The portions sitting on that shelf.
precise: A variable declared inside a class; every object has its own (in F2-09, Stock's portions_ and capacity_).
source: D2 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A function that belongs to a class and works on one object.
analogy: A task only the station's cook may do, such as "take portions".
precise: A function declared inside a class, called on an object (soup.take(4)); inside it, the members of that object are directly visible.
source: D1, D2 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Labels that say who may use a member.
analogy: The counter in front of the shelf: customers talk to the cook (public) but cannot reach the shelf (private).
precise: public members can be named anywhere; private members only inside the class's own member functions (and friends); the compiler rejects other uses.
source: D2 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-09

simple: A rule about an object's data that is true whenever someone outside can look.
analogy: The rule card taped to the shelf.
precise: A condition on the data members that the constructor establishes and every public member function preserves; it may be broken briefly inside a member function but must hold again when the function returns. See also the general invariant of MA102.
source: D1, D3 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The special function that sets up a new object.
analogy: The set-up checklist done before the station opens.
precise: A member function with the class's name and no return type, run when an object is created; it should establish the invariant or refuse to create the object (for example by throwing an exception, explained in F2-16). F2-10 covers constructors in depth.
source: D1, D2 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A tiny class that wraps one number so it cannot be confused with a different kind of number.
analogy: Putting grams on a scale and portions on a tally board, so nobody reads one as the other.
precise: A class such as Portions holding one int, with an explicit constructor, so that the compiler rejects passing a Grams where a Portions is required.
source: D3 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R4 of F2-09

simple: The special function that cleans up when an object's life ends.
analogy: The closing checklist of a station, which runs whenever the shift ends.
precise: A member function named ~ClassName(), with no parameters and no return type, called automatically at the end of the object's lifetime; for a local object, when control leaves its block by any path.
source: D1, D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R1 of F2-10

simple: The time from when an object is ready until it is cleaned up.
analogy: A station's shift, from the opening list to the closing list.
precise: The period from the end of the object's initialisation (its constructor finished) to the start of its destruction; a local object's lifetime ends when its enclosing block is left.
source: D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The part of the program between a pair of braces where a name can be used.
analogy: One room of the kitchen: what you set up in the room is cleared when you leave it.
precise: The region of source text in which a declaration is visible; for a local variable, from its declaration to the closing brace of the block.
source: D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The list after the colon in a constructor that gives each member its first value.
analogy: Setting each piece of equipment correctly as you put it on the station, instead of putting it wrong and fixing it later.
precise: The : a_(x), b_(y) part of a constructor definition; it initialises members before the constructor body runs.
source: D1, D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A starting value written next to the member itself.
analogy: A label on the shelf saying what goes there if nobody says otherwise.
precise: An initialiser in the member's declaration (int portions_ = 1;), used by any constructor that does not initialise that member in its own list.
source: D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-10

simple: The constructor used when you make an object without giving any values.
analogy: The standard opening list when nobody asks for anything special.
precise: A constructor that can be called with no arguments; Order() = default; asks the compiler to generate it.
source: D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The constructor that makes a new object as a copy of an existing one.
analogy: Photocopying an order ticket.
precise: A constructor taking const T&; if you do not declare one, the compiler generates one that copies each member, which is used, for example, when an object is passed by value. F2-13 treats copying in depth.
source: D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R5 of F2-10

simple: A way to say "this operation is forbidden" so the compiler refuses it.
analogy: A sign on the photocopier: "Do not copy tickets."
precise: A function declared with = delete; any use of it is a compile error.
source: D2 of F2-10 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R7 of F2-10

simple: Something your program borrows from the system and must give back.
analogy: A tool from the tool wall.
precise: Anything that must be acquired and later released: memory, open files, locks, network connections, GPU memory; if not released, it stays taken until the process ends.
source: D1, D3 of F2-11 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Tie a resource to an object: the object takes it when it is made and gives it back when it ends.
analogy: Borrowing a tool from the tool wall, which is returned automatically when you leave the room.
precise: The technique of acquiring a resource in a constructor and releasing it in the destructor of an owning object, so that the release happens on every path out of the owner's scope, including early returns and exceptions.
source: D1, D3 of F2-11 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R2 of F2-11

simple: A small number the operating system gives your program for each file it has open.
analogy: The number on the tag of a borrowed tool.
precise: On Linux and other POSIX systems, a non-negative integer returned by open() that indexes the process's table of open files; it stays valid until close() or the end of the process.
source: D4 of F2-11 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R5 of F2-11

simple: Taking a resource and never giving it back.
analogy: The spice key forgotten in an apron pocket.
precise: A resource acquired and never released while the program keeps running; leaks accumulate until acquisition fails.
source: lab runs R1, R5 of F2-11

simple: Leaving a function before its last line.
analogy: Leaving the room by the back door.
precise: A return statement before the end of a function body; any clean-up written after it does not run.
source: lab run R1 of F2-11

simple: A sign that says "I am using this; others must wait".
analogy: The single key to the spice cabinet.
precise: Here: a lock taken with Linux's flock() on an open file; it is held through that open file and released by flock(fd, LOCK_UN) or when the file is closed; "advisory" means only programs that also ask for the lock are stopped.
source: D4 of F2-11 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R6 of F2-11

simple: The one object responsible for giving a resource back.
analogy: The name written on the borrowing card.
precise: The object whose destructor releases the resource; with RAII each resource has exactly one owner at a time, which is why the wrapper forbids copying (F2-13 adds transfer of ownership by moving).
source: D3 of F2-11 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A second name for an object that already exists.
analogy: "The pot on burner two": not a bowl of stew, but a way to reach the pot itself.
precise: A declaration such as int& r = x; makes r an alias for the object x; it must be initialised, cannot be re-bound to another object, and every use of r uses x.
source: D1, D2 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R1 of F2-12

simple: The function gets its own copy of the argument.
analogy: A bowl ladled from the pot.
precise: The parameter is a new object initialised from the argument (for class types, by the copy constructor); changes to it do not affect the caller.
source: D2 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R2 of F2-12

simple: The function works on the caller's own object.
analogy: Stirring the actual pot.
precise: The parameter has reference type (T&) and is bound to the argument; no copy is made, and changes are visible to the caller.
source: D1 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R1 of F2-12

simple: A promise that something will not be changed, checked by the compiler.
analogy: "Look and taste, but add nothing."
precise: A type qualifier; an object or reference declared const cannot be modified through that name, and the compiler rejects attempts. See also const as first met in KID102.
source: D2 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-12

simple: A second name you may only read through.
analogy: Tasting from the pot with a promise not to add anything.
precise: A reference of type const T&; it avoids a copy and forbids modification through it; it can also bind to temporaries.
source: D1, D2 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A member function that promises not to change its object.
analogy: The cook's "check the stock" job, which only looks.
precise: A member function declared with const after its parameter list; inside it, the object is treated as const; only const member functions can be called on a const object or through a const reference.
source: D2 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-12

simple: A reference to an object that no longer exists.
analogy: A note saying "pot on burner two" after the pot was moved.
precise: A reference whose object's lifetime has ended; using it is undefined behaviour.
source: D2 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R5 of F2-12

simple: Something the C++ rules do not allow, so anything may happen, including "seems to work".
analogy: Tasting from an empty burner: maybe nothing, maybe someone else's dish.
precise: Behaviour for which the standard imposes no requirements; SP201 (F2-23) treats it in depth.
source: D2 of F2-12 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Make a second, independent object with the same value.
analogy: A photocopy of the recipe card.
precise: Done by the copy constructor (T(const T&)) or copy assignment (T& operator=(const T&)); afterwards the two objects are equal and changing one does not change the other.
source: D1 of F2-13 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R2 of F2-13

simple: Hand the contents of an object over to another, leaving the first one empty or reusable.
analogy: Handing over the original card.
precise: Done by the move constructor (T(T&&)) or move assignment (T& operator=(T&&)), which may take resources from the source; the source stays a valid object, in a state each class documents.
source: D1, D2 of F2-13 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R7 of F2-13

simple: A label that says "you may take this object's contents".
analogy: Writing "please take the original" on the card.
precise: A function in <utility> that only converts its argument to an rvalue reference so that a move operation can be chosen; it moves nothing by itself.
source: D1, D2 of F2-13 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A kind of reference that binds to things that are about to disappear or that were marked with std::move.
analogy: The tray marked "leftovers: take whatever you need".
precise: A reference type written T&&; overloads taking T&& are chosen for temporaries and for std::move(x), which is how the compiler picks moving over copying.
source: D2 of F2-13 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: What is left in an object after its contents were moved away.
analogy: The empty hook where the card used to hang.
precise: The state of the source after a move; for standard library types, "valid but unspecified" (you may assign to it or destroy it, but should not rely on its value); your own classes should document it (our File: owns nothing).
source: D2, D3 of F2-13 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

term: Rule of zero / rule of five
simple: Either write none of the copy, move and destructor functions, or think about all five.
analogy: Either follow the standard kitchen procedure fully, or write your own procedure for every step.
precise: Guidelines: let members that manage themselves (std::string, std::vector, RAII wrappers) give correct behaviour with no declarations (zero); if a class must declare any of destructor, copy constructor, copy assignment, move constructor, move assignment, it should declare or delete all five.
source: D3 of F2-13 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The compiler building the result directly where it is needed, with no copy and no move.
analogy: Writing the card straight onto the cook's hook instead of writing it elsewhere and moving it.
precise: Since C++17, returning a temporary (return T(...);) used to initialise an object constructs it in place, without calling copy or move constructors.
source: D2 of F2-13 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R1 of F2-13

simple: Code with a blank that the compiler fills in with a type or a number.
analogy: A recipe card "stir-fry with ______".
precise: A declaration introduced by template <...> that defines a family of functions or classes, parameterised by types or values.
source: D1, D2 of F2-14 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The blank in a template.
analogy: The empty line on the card.
precise: A name declared in the template's parameter list: a type parameter (typename T) or a non-type parameter such as std::size_t N.
source: D2 of F2-14 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The compiler writing the real code for one filled-in blank.
analogy: Writing out "stir-fry with tofu" as a real recipe.
precise: The generation of a concrete function or class from a template for specific arguments, for example larger<int>; each instantiation is separate code.
source: D2 of F2-14 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R6 of F2-14

simple: The compiler working out what to put in the blank from the values you pass.
analogy: Seeing tofu in the pan and knowing which card version is meant.
precise: For a function template call without explicit arguments, the compiler deduces the template arguments from the argument types; conflicting deductions are an error.
source: D2 of F2-14 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R2 of F2-14

simple: A named rule for what a type must be able to do.
analogy: A note on the card: "fill only with something that can be fried".
precise: A C++20 named set of requirements on template arguments, such as std::totally_ordered; a template constrained by a concept is not used for types that fail it, and the error says which requirement failed.
source: D2 of F2-14 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R4 of F2-14

simple: A check that runs while compiling.
analogy: The head chef refusing a card with an impossible blank before anyone cooks.
precise: A declaration static_assert(condition, message); if the constant condition is false, compilation fails with the message.
source: D2 of F2-14 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R8 of F2-14

simple: A queue in a fixed number of slots that wraps around from the last slot to the first.
analogy: The loop of clips on the order rail.
precise: A first-in, first-out buffer of capacity N stored in an array; a head index marks the oldest element and a count (or tail index) marks how many are stored; indices advance modulo N.
source: D3 of F2-14 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R7 of F2-14

simple: A thing that points at one element of a container and can move to the next.
analogy: A finger on a jar of the spice shelf.
precise: An object that supports at least *it (the element) and ++it (the next element), and can be compared with another iterator; stronger categories add --, jumps such as it + n, and contiguous storage.
source: D1, D2 of F2-15 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: "From this element up to, but not including, that one".
analogy: From the first jar to the painted line after the last jar.
precise: A pair of iterators [first, last); first is included, last is not, and first == last means an empty range. end() is one past the last element and must not be dereferenced.
source: D2 of F2-15 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R1 of F2-15

simple: A ready-made procedure from the standard library that works on any range.
analogy: A page in the kitchen's procedure book.
precise: A function template in <algorithm> or <numeric> that operates on a range given by iterators (or, in std::ranges, by a whole container), with documented complexity.
source: D1, D2 of F2-15 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A function that answers yes or no about an element.
analogy: The question "is this order quick?" asked of each ticket.
precise: A callable returning a value convertible to bool, passed to algorithms such as std::count_if; a comparison function for std::sort must define a strict weak ordering.
source: D2 of F2-15 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: Telling a ranges algorithm which part of each element to look at.
analogy: "Sort the tickets, but read only the table number."
precise: An extra argument of the std::ranges algorithms, such as a pointer to member &Order::table, applied to each element before comparing.
source: D2 of F2-15 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-15

simple: Removing elements in two steps: move the keepers forward, then cut off the tail.
analogy: Sliding the good jars to the left, then taking the leftover jars off the end of the shelf.
precise: v.erase(std::remove(v.begin(), v.end(), x), v.end()); since C++20, std::erase(v, x) does both.
source: D2 of F2-15 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R6 of F2-15

simple: A returned value that says whether it worked, and if not, why.
analogy: A note handed back: "unreadable", "no cream".
precise: A return value (often an enum class) whose values name the outcomes; the result itself is returned separately, for example through a reference parameter.
source: D3 of F2-16 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R1 of F2-16

simple: A box that holds either a value or nothing.
analogy: A plate that may come back empty.
precise: The class template std::optional<T> (header <optional>), which contains a T or is empty (std::nullopt); test it with if (o) and read it with *o or o.value_or(default).
source: D2 of F2-16 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R1 of F2-16

simple: A way to stop the normal work and jump to code that can handle the problem.
analogy: The alarm to the manager.
precise: An object thrown with throw; control leaves the current function and continues at the nearest matching catch handler of an enclosing try block.
source: D1, D2 of F2-16 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: On the way out, every function that is left behind tidies up.
analogy: Each station turns off its burners as the cooks leave.
precise: While an exception travels to its handler, the destructors of all automatic objects in the scopes it leaves run, in reverse order of construction.
source: D2 of F2-16 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R2 of F2-16

simple: The emergency stop when nobody handles an exception.
analogy: The alarm rings and no manager answers: the building is evacuated.
precise: The function called when an exception is not caught (and in a few other cases); by default it calls std::abort, which ends the program with the signal SIGABRT.
source: D2 of F2-16 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-16

simple: A label that says "do not ignore what this function returns".
analogy: A note stapled to the ticket that must be read.
precise: An attribute on a function or type; discarding the returned value causes a compiler warning, which -Werror turns into an error.
source: D2 of F2-16 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R4 of F2-16

simple: What is still true about your objects after an exception went through.
analogy: After the alarm, are the stations safe and the stock lists correct?
precise: The basic guarantee: no leaks and every invariant holds; the strong guarantee: the operation either succeeds or changes nothing; no-throw: it never throws (noexcept).
source: D1, D3 of F2-16 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A small function written exactly where you need it.
analogy: A sticky-note instruction.
precise: An expression [captures](parameters) { body } that creates an unnamed function object; the return type is usually deduced.
source: D1, D2 of F2-17 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: The object a lambda expression creates.
analogy: The note itself, with whatever was written on it.
precise: An object of a unique, compiler-generated class type, whose data members hold the captured values and whose operator() runs the body.
source: D2 of F2-17 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab runs R2, R4 of F2-17

simple: What a lambda takes with it from the place where it was written.
analogy: A number copied onto the note, or "the board by the door".
precise: An entry in the capture list: [x] copies x into the closure (by value); [&x] refers to the original x (by reference); [n = expr] creates a new member initialised from expr.
source: D2 of F2-17 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A box that can hold any function-like thing with a given signature.
analogy: A holder on the wall that takes any note saying "do this with a table number".
precise: The class template std::function<R(Args...)> (header <functional>), which stores a copy of any callable with that signature and calls it through one interface.
source: D2 of F2-17 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-17

simple: A function you give to someone else so they can call it later.
analogy: "When the bell rings, do this."
precise: A callable passed to and stored by other code, which invokes it when an event happens.
source: D1 of F2-17 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R3 of F2-17

simple: A lambda that works for many types.
analogy: A note with a blank, like the recipe card of F2-14.
precise: A lambda with auto parameters; its operator() is a member function template, instantiated per argument type.
source: D2 of F2-17 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open); lab run R4 of F2-17

simple: A rule about the state that is always true between operations.
analogy: The station's rule card: portions are never fewer than 0 and never more than the shelf holds.
precise: A condition on the state that holds before and after every operation; in a class, a class invariant established by the constructor and kept by every public member function.
source: D3 of F2-09 (title only; pending verification, dossier gate G1 open)

simple: A function that runs code with known inputs and checks the results.
analogy: Tasting a dish against the recipe card before it leaves the kitchen.
precise: A function that calls the code under test with known inputs, compares the results with expected values and reports failures; SP102's labs use an expect(condition, what) helper that counts failures and sets the exit code.
source: lab runs of the SP102 lab reference solutions (F2-09 to F2-17)
